paragraphs: Chapter 919
Episode 229. Kelliark's Safety Mechanism (2)
"True. But right now?"
"Phaelito will soon have to go to the surface under Zito's orders, so there isn't much time. He would have liked to take more time, but it can't be helped now."
"I understand."

"As the situation is turbulent, even you would need a justification to meet Phaelito directly. Contact Geomma Castle, reveal that this is Dokma Castle, and tell them there's something to report about me."

Raela took out the seal of the Belgasium family from her possession. A small dimensional gate floated above the darkly drawn seal as it began to absorb mana. The landscape of the Steward's Office at Geomma Castle was visible beyond the dimensional gate.
{Lord Raela, what can I do for you?}
"Is the Geomma in the castle?"
{Yes, do you wish to see Geomma?}
"Yes."
{As you know... Geomma is very upset over the death of the archivist.}
"I know. But there's urgent information about Ragal Pun and the prisoner he was in charge of. Open the gate. And until I enter and see Lord Phaelito, ensure that no one can see me and the prisoner."
{Please wait a moment.}
The steward of Geomma Castle disappeared for about ten seconds before reappearing.
{I will open the gate now. I will set the coordinates to the front of Geomma's office. Entry for Lord Raela and Ragal's prisoner, a total of 2 persons. Is that correct?}
"Yes."
Whoosh!
The seal vibrated and the dimensional gate widened. As soon as Raela and Kelliark stepped inside, they saw the door to Phaelito's office immediately.
Raela's expression hardened, as if she was a little nervous.
"Geomma, it's Raela."
"...Come in."
As soon as the door opened, a thick magic aura emerged. The sorrow over Sakiel's death, and the resentment and hatred for the ones who killed her were continuously amplifying Phaelito's magic.
Phaelito was controlling himself so that his magic would not harm others. His expressionless face, as he sat in silence, was imbued with a deep sorrow like an abyss.
Raela bowed her head deeply and waited for Phaelito to speak first.
"Raela, at some point, I forgot how long I've lived."
After a while, Phaelito opened his mouth, not even looking at Kelliark Zipple standing next to Raela.

"Thousands of years, tens of thousands of years, or perhaps even longer. Like other demons, I too have passed through numerous cycles of oblivion, losing many memories. I cannot remember at all why I opposed Lord Zito in the past, what I was trying to protect from him..."
"Lord Phaelito..."
Phaelito opened his eyes.

"But in the fuzzy, distant life, there was always one thing that was clear. That was, in Lord Zito's reign... The task of raising the demon world where Sakiel and I belong to the rightful land. Just like the surface where humans, who have no qualifications whatsoever, are enjoying the real sun."
Tears of crimson flowed from Phaelito's red eyes. It was the first time Leila had seen him cry. At least as far as Leila could remember.
"Sakiel is dead."
"I... know."

"Sakiel single-handedly raised the Guroshega, was the general who best defended against those who opposed Lord Zito, and the unparalleled general who stabilized the savage political situation of the demon world. And to me... To me, she was more than a subordinate. A comrade who together made this land prosperous, a fellow who aimed for the same fate. Such Sakiel was brutally torn apart and killed by humans."
Swoosh!
Suddenly, the sharp energy emanating from Phaelito grazed Kelliark's cheek. Kelliark did not wipe the flowing blood, nor looked at Phaelito.

"Kelliark Zipple, it must be clear why a human like you became a prisoner of Ragal. You did well not to meet my eyes now. Otherwise, I would have cut your throat. Even with the witch behind you, to my eyes now, you just look like a human who must be exterminated."

"Indeed, is this the power of the Royal Sword Bascal? It's just a shallow wound on the cheek, but my body feels chilly with the sensation of blocked power. If killing me would relieve your grief a little, then Bescio, don't stop him."
"You talk as if it's possible to block my sword."
"If it's a sword that has lost its cool, sure. But if it's a real Sword Master's sword, it would be difficult to avoid, even if it's not Bascal."
"Hehehehe..."
Phaelito let out a hollow laugh.
The raging magic from him suddenly became calm, and the tear marks on his cheeks disappeared without a trace.
"I see why you've come to Sword Demon Castle now. So... the witch wants me to kill humans more calmly?"
"The witch, and Lord Zito, wouldn't want that. Your grace should now go to the surface to avenge Sakiel Guroshega and retrieve Lord Zito's body."
For a while, Phaelito stared at Kelliark with deep, dark eyes.
"Kelliark Zipple."
"Speak."

"There's no way that Lord Zito himself sent you, who is the puppet of the witch, to me. Your visit here must entirely be the will of the witch. So go and tell the witch, tell her that you have calmed me down."
"From my perspective, Your Highness, you still haven't completely calmed down."
Every time Kelliark opened his mouth, Raella felt a dry feeling in her stomach. Every single word was a dangerous statement.
Phaelito was reading Raella's mind accurately.

"It's okay, Raella. I was going crazy with the grief of losing Sakielle, but suddenly my head cools down. This is why everyone avoids the witch. No matter what, once you get involved with the witch even a little bit, the situation definitely goes the way she wants it to."
Raella bowed her head again. She felt like she was finally facing the familiar image of Phaelito.
Even that was painful to the heart, as it was a distorted image brainwashed by Zito.
'When did Zito's brainwashing start. We are, when did we...'
Phaelito got up and took a slow, deep breath.
"So, how can I further calm my heart from here? Kelliark Zipple."
Kelliark took something out of his pocket.
It was a black bead. It's condensed with extremely pure soul energy.
"This is a bead made by Witch Hellurum. The witch hopes that you will possess this before you go into the decisive battle with Insae."
"What is it used for?"
"It depends on what you wish to use it for. If you want life, it can give you life, if you want death, it can give you death."
"The explanation is vague."
"The witch is always like that."
Phaelito stared at the bead with calm eyes. It felt as if if he looked into it for a long time, he would be sucked into it and never come out.

"But if I were to interpret the witch's will, life probably symbolizes escape. If you're ever in danger of dying during the battle, you can escape somewhere by using this bead. I think, probably, it would be Lord Zito's dwelling."
"Why do you think so?"

"What else could be the reason the witch sent you to me? She probably hopes you don't fail. So shouldn't she save you if you're going to die? The moment you are defeated by Insae's warriors, the safest place in Hell would be Lord Zito's dwelling."

"Then death would mean a self-destruct mechanism. Like... how Sakielle did it. Does the witch believe that I will lose to the warriors of Insae? That I would go into the battle without calming my heart?"

"Perhaps. If you are not fighting as a perfect Archdemon, I would make the same judgment. Archdemon, ascension. In the world of Insae, it means a level that is never affected by emotions. But what I saw of you today is far from that. You were sad, and you still are."
Phaelito picked up the bead placed on Kelliark's palm.
"I'll take it."
"A wise decision."
"How do you use it?"

"Think of what you want and shatter the orb. Anyway, the fact that the witch gave you the orb means she probably wants to save you in a pinch. I hope you fight not as someone who has lost a companion, but as the Sword Demon Paerlito. Then you won't have to use this orb."
"That's an interesting thing to say. From the perspective of someone who serves the witch, it would be best for you if I use this orb in any way."
At those words, Kelliark bowed his head with a bitter face.
"I am not a servant of the witch. Didn't you just say it yourself? That's why everyone avoids the witch."
"Ah, so you're in the same boat, being played by the witch's tricks."
"That's the way it is."
"Whether your words are true or not, we will know after the fight is over. You may leave now."
Paerlito turned around.
Leila barely swallowed the words that had come up to her throat, "Good luck".
"...... I wish you luck, Sword Demon."
"Leila."
"Speak your mind."
"Do you know when the next cycle of oblivion is?"
"I do not know."
"I don't either. So we live lives where we can lose someone at any time."
Unable to choose a reply, Leila had to leave the office.
Then, while escaping from the Sword Demon Castle, no one in the castle was able to directly confirm the presence of Leila and Kelliark.
"Indeed, I couldn't rid the brainwashing through the fire of awakening. If I had used that power, I would have had to fight Paerlito."
"Is that orb really from the witch? In case the Sword Demon is stabbed by the daggers of the humans, can it really save the Sword Demon?"

"That orb was made by me, not the witch. It was made mainly from chaos, so it can be said that I borrowed the power of the witch. The effect is also different from the explanation. The orb only has the function of escape."
"What, then you lied to the Sword Demon?"
"Would Paerlito have accepted it if I said that I made the orb?"
"That's a good point. But wouldn't it have been better to tell him that it only has the escape function?"

"The witch is an ambiguous and confusing existence. Would the witch make something just to rescue someone from danger? If I had explained it that way, Paerlito would not have believed it. Especially since he has met the witch several times with Zito."
"Ah, I understand. So no matter what choice the Sword Demon makes when cornered, he just needs to shatter the orb."
"That's right. Isn't this quite a good safety measure?"
Leila nodded.
Kelliark quietly smiled, imagining Paerlito shattering the orb.
